purpose: Source explanation for a separate post-hoc observed paired heap overhead analysis. This does not change the original failed absolute-heap protocol or establish exact live heap.
source_binary_relation: The measured build pins this release RTS artifact from this SDK worktree; the source excerpts match the recorded SDK commit. This analysis verifies those files and artifact hashes, not a new reproducible RTS build.

weak_registry_mark_stack.expression: same MarkStack allocation, even when no Weak values are present

explanation: The trigger replies without Candid allocation, then forces an incremental_gc call. A trigger can start, advance or finish a cycle; no authoritative cycle counter was recorded.
Marking starts with a fresh ordinary MarkStack. complete_marking unconditionally accesses the weak-reference registry, lazily constructing another stack and its container even without Weak values.
Evacuation planning allocates a temporary ranking array with one 8-byte index per partition. This workload uses the initial 128-entry partition table.

Every allocation above uses managed Blob storage. Temporary GC objects become garbage; the current allocation partition is excluded from evacuation, so repeated forced cycles can increase occupied heap.

The source-derived 17504 bytes exactly matches each observed total-allocation increment across all modes, stages, trials and 24 forced-trigger positions. Beyond the first trigger in each stage, occupied heap also rises by 17504 bytes with no new reclaim.

Consequently the original absolute 4096-byte tail-spread criterion fails in every mode. Pairing each prepared sample with its baseline at the same trial/stage/trigger index cancels the observed identical bookkeeping contribution; this remains a post-hoc observational comparison, not exact live-heap measurement.

let export_gc_trigger_method env =
    let name = IC.gc_trigger_method_name in
    begin match E.mode env with
    | Flags.ICMode ->
      Func.define_built_in env name [] [] (fun env ->
        (* THe GC trigger is also blocked during incremental (de)stabilization.
           This is checked in `Lifecycle.trans` being called by `message_start` *)
        message_start env (Type.Shared Type.Write) ^^
        (* Check that we are called from this or a controller, w/o allocation *)
        IC.assert_caller_self_or_controller env ^^
        (* To avoid more failing allocation, don't deserialize args nor serialize reply,
           i.e. don't even try to do this:
        Serialization.deserialize env [] ^^
        Tuple.compile_unit env ^^
        Serialization.serialize env [] ^^
        *)
        (* Instead, just ignore the argument and
           send a *statically* allocated, nullary reply *)
        IC.static_nullary_reply env ^^
        (* Finally, act like
        message_cleanup env (Type.Shared Type.Write)
           but *force* collection *)
        GC.record_mutator_instructions env ^^
        E.collect_garbage env true ^^
        GC.record_collector_instructions env ^^
        Lifecycle.trans env Lifecycle.Idle
      );

      let fi = E.built_in env name in
